It is a shikinaisha and the ichinomiya of {{ill|Suō Province|cs|Provincie Suó|de|Provinz Suō|es|Provincia de Suō|fa|ولایت سوئو|fr|Province de Suō|gl|Provincia de Suō|id|Provinsi Suō|it|Suō (provincia)|ja|周防国|ko|스오국|lt|Suo žemė|nl|Suo (provincie)|pt|Província de Suō|ru|Суо (провинция)|simple|Suō Province|sk|Suó (provincia)|sr|Провинција Суо|tr|Suō (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Суо|uz|Suo viloyati|wuu|周防国|zh|周防國|zh_min_nan|Suô-kok|qid=Q1053037}}. Its former modern rank was kokuhei chusha; today it is a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|ja|別表神社|mr|बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|simple|Beppyo shrine|zh|別表神社|qid=Q10898274}} of Jinja Honcho. {{nihongo|'''Tamanooya Shrine'''|玉祖神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. It is located in [[Suo Province]].

It is regarded as the head shrine of Tamanooya shrines, including other Tamanooya shrines in Hofu and {{ill|Tamanooya Shrine|ja|玉祖神社 (八尾市)|qid=Q11572730}} in Osaka.

== Enshrined deities ==
* {{ill|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|it|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|ja|玉祖命|zh|玉祖命|qid=Q11572729}} - ancestral deity of the Tamatsukuri clan; deity associated with making magatama at the time of the Heavenly Rock Cave myth.
* One additional deity (unidentified; some theories suggest {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto}} or {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Kagami-no-Mikoto}})

== History ==
The shrine is thought to have been founded by jewel-crafting groups (tamatsukuri-be) who worshiped Tamanooya-no-Mikoto. According to one tradition, Emperor Keiko prayed for victory here during his western campaign.

Shrine tradition says Tamanooya-no-Mikoto died in this area and was enshrined here; nearby is "Tama no Iwaya," said to be the deity's tomb. In the Heian period it was revered as the ichinomiya of Suo. In modern times it was ranked kokuhei shosha in 1871 and promoted to kokuhei chusha in 1915; after WWII it became a Beppyo shrine.

The monk {{ill|Chōgen (monk)|de|Chōgen|fr|Chōgen|ja|重源|qid=Q679462}} is said to have donated shrine buildings and tax-exempt lands in 1195 in thanks for completion of work connected to reconstruction of {{ill|Tōdai-ji|ar|توداي-جي|arz|تودائى جى|ca|Tōdai-ji|cs|Tódaidži|de|Tōdai-ji|el|Τοντάι Τσι|eo|Tōdai-ji|es|Tōdai-ji|eu|Tōdai-ji|fa|تودای‌جی|fi|Tōdai-ji|fr|Tōdai-ji|gan|東大寺|he|טודאי-ג'י|hi|तोडाई-जी|hu|Tódaidzsi|id|Tōdai-ji|it|Tōdai-ji|ja|東大寺|ka|ტოდაი-ძი|ko|도다이지|la|Tōdai-ji|ms|Tōdai-ji|my|တိုးဒိုင်းဂျိ|nl|Todai-ji|no|Tōdai-ji|pl|Tōdai-ji|pt|Tōdai-ji|rki|တိုးဒအိ ဘုရားကျောင်း|ro|Tōdai-ji|ru|Тодай-дзи|sh|Tōdai-ji|simple|Tōdai-ji|sl|Todai-dži|sr|Тодаиђи|th|โทไดจิ|tok|tomo sewi Totawi|tr|Tōdai-ji|uk|Монастир Тодай|vi|Chùa Tōdai|wuu|东大寺|zh|东大寺|zh_yue|東大寺|qid=Q460367}}. The shrine preserves an Important Cultural Property document bearing Chogen's signature.

== Divine rank ==
* 867-03-10: raised from Junior Fourth Rank, Lower to Junior Third Rank (recorded as "Tamanooya no Kami")
* 964: recorded as Junior First Rank

== Major rituals ==
On the evening before the autumn festival, the "Urate" ritual is performed; early on festival day, a rice-offering rite using earthen kettles is held. Both are linked to a tradition that Empress Jingu divined military fortune at this shrine before the Sankan campaign. The sumo-like Urate performance is also called "Urate-zumo" and is designated as an intangible folk cultural property of Yamaguchi Prefecture.

== Cultural properties ==
== Important Cultural Property (National) ==
* "Inventory of shrine buildings and treasures for reconstruction of Suo ichinomiya" (dated 1195, signed by Chogen) - designated June 5, 1976

== Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property (National selection) ==
* Urate sumo of Tamanooya Shrine - selected December 4, 1997

== Yamaguchi Prefecture designated cultural property ==
* Urate ritual of Tamanooya Shrine (intangible folk cultural property) - designated November 24, 1976

== Hofu City designated cultural properties ==
* Two swords (craft works) designated March 31, 1969
* Shrine forest designated natural monument (March 3, 1986)

== Other ==
The shrine is also associated with the origin of the locally designated natural-monument breed "Kurokashiwa chicken"; a monument stands in the precinct and several are kept there.

== Access ==
* JR Sanyo Main Line Hofu Station: about 45 minutes on foot
* Bocho bus "Sogo Iryo Center-mae" stop: about 20 minutes on foot
